paragraphs.heading: What a stem is
paragraphs.text: A stem is one of the two main axes that give a vascular plant its structure; the root is the other. It holds up leaves, flowers and fruits and carries water, and substances dissolved in it, between roots and shoots. It also takes part in photosynthesis, stores nutrients and makes new living tissue. The woody stem of a tree is its trunk, and a stem may also be called a stalk, culm or haulm.

paragraphs.heading: Nodes, internodes and buds
paragraphs.text: Leaves join the stem at points called nodes, and one node can carry a single leaf or several. The stretch of stem between two nodes is an internode, and depending on the species it can lengthen from its base or from its tip. Between a leaf and the stem there is sometimes an axillary bud that can grow into a branch bearing leaves, cones or flowers. Nodes can also sprout adventitious roots, such as brace roots, and vines may send out tendrils from them.

paragraphs.heading: Two pipelines and a divider
paragraphs.text: Inside the stem run two pipe-like tissues, xylem and phloem. Xylem forms on the inner side and carries water, moved by transpiration pull, capillary action and root pressure. Phloem forms on the outer side, is made of sieve tubes with their companion cells, and spreads food from the photosynthetic tissue to the rest of the plant. Between the two lies the cambium, a tissue whose cells divide to make new xylem or phloem cells.

paragraphs.heading: Keeping the plant going
paragraphs.text: Stems hold the leaves up in the light, which photosynthesis depends on, and give the plant somewhere to carry its flowers and fruits. They also store nutrients so the plant can reach them when it runs short. Plant cells usually live only one to three years. Stems contain meristems, cells that produce new living tissue every year.

paragraphs.heading: Stems under the ground
paragraphs.text: In most plants the stem grows above the soil, but some plants keep it underground. A bulb is a short, upright underground stem wrapped in fleshy storage leaves, as in the onion, daffodil and tulip. Because the leaves make up most of it, a bulb might better be thought of as leaves. Bulbs often multiply by splitting or by making small new bulbs called bulblets. A corm is a short, swollen underground stem used for storage, found in taro, crocus and gladiolus.

paragraphs.heading: Stems in disguise
paragraphs.text: Some stems hardly look like stems. A cactus pad is a cladode, a flat stem that looks like a leaf and does photosynthesis. Rose thorns are prickles, sharp outgrowths of the stem's outer layers. Some Viola species seem to have no stem at all, but their stems are simply very short, so the leaves appear to rise straight from the ground. The banana has a pseudostem, a false stem of rolled-up leaf bases that can reach 2 to 3 m.
